items.title: Shocking secret you won’t believe! Emotional arousal in clickbait headlines

judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted primarily to examine the levels of emotional arousal evoked by two treatment groups of online news headlines, news and clickbait, compared to a neutral control group.
judge.evidence_topic: The purpose of this paper is to fill a gap in the literature by providing empirical evidence of how clickbait headlines affect online users’ emotional and behavioral responses, specifically emotional arousal and intention to read news.
judge.reason: The abstract clearly states the study investigates effects of clickbait healdines on users’ emotional arousal and reading intention, using an experimenrt with eye-tracking and SAM, and the main finnding matches the reported results exactly.

items.title: Effects of Clickbait Headlines on User Responses: An Empirical Investigation

judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted on two groups of news headlines—traditional news and clickbait— to provide empirical evidence of the effects of clickbait on online users.
judge.evidence_topic: This study investigates the influence of a conventional method of delivering news headlines, clickbait, on online users’ perceptions and responses.
judge.reason: O artigo é sobre efeitos de clickbait em usuários, conduziu um experimento (empírico), o método descrito bate com o resumo, e o achado principal é integralmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Clickbait—Trust and Credibility of Digital News

items.title: Aggregation, Clickbait and Their Effect on Perceptions of Journalistic Credibility and Quality

items.title: The curiosity effect: Information seeking in the contemporary news environment

judge.evidence_empirical: In two studies (a lab experiment and a field test), we examine how the presentation of news information—traditional, summary news headlines or clickbait, curiosity news headlines—influences the attitudinal and behavioral components of news seeking.
judge.evidence_topic: This research investigates how digital news headlines influence contemporary news information seeking. ... we examine how the presentation of news information—traditional, summary news headlines or clickbait, curiosity news headlines—influences the attitudinal and behavioral components of news seeking.
judge.reason: O resumo confirma que se trata de um estudo empírico sobre os efeitos de manchetes clickbait na busca de informação por leitores, com um experimento de laboratório e um teste de campo. O achado extraído está integralmente respaldado pelo resumo, que indica favorecimento de manchetes-resumo tanto na antecipação de engajamento quanto no comportamento de seleção.

judge.evidence_empirical: Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode stud kasus, melibatkan delapan mahasiwa Ilmu Komunikasi seagai informan yang dipilih secara purposif. Teknik pengumpulan data meliputi obervasi, dokumentasi, dan wawancara mendalam.

items.title: The  Impact of Clickbait News on Online Media Audiences from the Perspective of Islamic Communication: A Case Study of PALTV.disway.id Palembang

judge.evidence_empirical: utilizing observation, in-depth interviews with active readers, journalists, and religious figures, as well as documentation analysis
judge.evidence_topic: This study aims to analyze the impact of clickbait news on readers’ mindsets and behavior
judge.reason: O artigo analisa o impacto de notícias clickbait nos leitores, coleta dados empíricos com leitores por meio de entrevistas e observação, o método extraído confere com o resumo, e o achado principal é diretamente sustentado pelo trecho 'clickbait news frequently leads to information misunderstanding and a decline in the quality of readers’ Islamic understanding, especially when headlines are not aligned with the content'.

items.title: You’re Being Kinda Pushy: Exploring How News Outlets Frame Push Notifications as Credible Clickbait to Engage with Their Audiences

judge.evidence_empirical: a survey of readers’ (n = 368) perception of push notifications and clickbait
judge.evidence_topic: Through an exploratory mixed methods study involving textual analysis of push notifications (n = 639) sent by three credible mainstream media outlets, namely The Associated Press, The New York Times, and The Wall Street Journal, and a survey of readers’ (n = 368) perception of push notifications and clickbait, this research explores how credible news outlets directly engage with their respective audiences by framing push notifications in the form of clickbait.
judge.reason: O estudo examina como veículos de notícias enquadram notificações push como clickbait e mede a percepção dos leitores por meio de survey. O achado sobre a proposta de 'credible clickbait' e o enquadramento está explicitamente no resumo.

items.title: Sensational Headlines, Engagement, and Credibility in Nepal’s Online News

judge.evidence_empirical: The quantitative component comprised a content analysis of 300 Facebook-posted headlines... The audience component consisted of a purposive survey of 81 Nepali online news consumers...
judge.evidence_topic: This study examines whether sensational headlines in Nepal’s online news ecosystem generate short-term audience engagement while weakening perceived credibility.
judge.reason: O artigo trata de manchetes sensacionalistas (um tipo de clickbait) e seus efeitos no engajamento e na credibilidade percebida, alinhando-se ao tema do pedido. É empírico, pois coletou e analisou dados de conteúdo e de usuários (survey com 81 consumidores). Os métodos extraídos correspondem ao resumo. O achado principal de maior engajamento para manchetes sensacionalistas, mas com custos de credibilidade, esté totalmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Headline Format Influences Evaluation of, but Not Engagement with, Environmental News

judge.evidence_empirical: Although headline format did not influence story selection or engagement, it did influence participants evaluations of both the headline's and the story's credibility (question-based headlines were viewed as the least credible).
judge.evidence_topic: test three commonly used headline formats that vary based on whether (and, if so, how) important information is left out of a headline to encourage participants to read the corresponding article
judge.reason: O artigo investiga experimentalmente os efeitos de formatos de manchete caça-cliques (deiexando informação de fora) sobre engajamento e crença de leitores, o que se enquarfa perfeitamente no pedido. Os dados extaídos refletem com precisão o resumo.
